In 1939, every school bus in America was a different color. And they kept disappearing.
Red buses vanished at sunset. Dark ones melted into the fog.
So a professor named Frank Cyr pinned about fifty paint colors to a wall.
But at dusk, red turns dark gray, and blends into the road.
Cyr picked yellow orange instead. Your eyes catch it fast, even from the corner of your eye.
Black letters pop on it too. Eventually, every state used it.
The rival painted his car red. Nobody saw it at sunset.
